wave_title: Ninth fix this generation cycle. gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to spelling.rs's OTHER spelling functions for the same 'syn's AST structurally drops a syntactic distinction' pattern just fixed for tuples. Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read type_spelling's real Type::Path arm directly (confirmed it reads only type_path.path, never type_path.qself), read syn 3.0.6's own real source (ty.rs's TypePath struct definition, path.rs's QSelf struct definition) directly from the vendored crate on disk to confirm qself.ty genuinely holds the qualifying type separately from path.segments -- not trusting the subagent's description of syn's internals alone -- and traced the consequence through TypeIdentity::identity_key() exactly as done for the prior tuple fix.
key_finding: For a qualified/associated-type path like `<A as Container>::Item`, `syn::TypePath` is `{ attrs, qself: Option<QSelf>, path: Path }` where `qself.ty` holds the qualifying type (`A`) and `path.segments` holds only the trailing trait/item segments (`["Container", "Item"]`) -- the qualifying type is NOT itself a path segment. `type_spelling`'s `Type::Path` arm read only `type_path.path` via `path_spelling(&type_path.path)`, never `type_path.qself`, so `<A as Container>::Item` and `<B as Container>::Item` -- two genuinely different types (the same associated type projected through two different trait implementations) -- both spelled to the identical string `"Container::Item"`. Since this feeds `TypeIdentity.name` directly and `TypeIdentity.canonical` stays `None` throughout this extractor's scope, `identity_key()` hashes on `name` alone -- so both types collapsed onto the exact same `TypeIdentity` record_id and graph Type node whenever they appeared in the same scope (e.g. two functions in the same module each taking a parameter of one of these associated types).
verification_before_acting: Read type_spelling's real Type::Path arm directly, confirming it reads only type_path.path, never type_path.qself.

Read the actual vendored syn 3.0.6 source on disk (ty.rs's TypePath struct, path.rs's QSelf struct) directly -- not the subagent's description -- confirming qself.ty is a real, separate field holding the qualifying type, structurally absent from path.segments.

Traced the consequence through TypeIdentity's real identity_key() implementation (unchanged since the prior generation's fix, still hashing on name alone with canonical always None), confirming this is a genuine cross-type identity collision reaching the graph, not a cosmetic display nit.

Independently constructed and ran the exact colliding snippet (<A as Container>::Item vs <B as Container>::Item) against the real, unfixed extractor code before writing the fix, confirming both produced the byte-identical string "Container::Item".

Evaluated the subagent's secondary, lower-confidence finding (pattern_spelling's Pat::Ident arm dropping by_ref/mutability, so x/mut x/ref x all render "x") and independently confirmed via reading FunctionIdentity::identity_key() and the engineering-graph HAS_PARAMETER_TYPE edge construction that parameter.name is never part of any identity_key() -- only parameter.type_identity.identity_key() is -- so this does not clear the same identity-collision bar and was correctly not treated as a defect this generation.

design_decisions.question: Hand-implement syn's qself/path-splitting rendering logic, or fall back to the token stream?
design_decisions.decision: Fall back to the raw token stream (guard the Type::Path arm on qself.is_none(), letting a Some(_) qself fall through to the existing catch-all `other => other.to_token_stream().to_string()`), rather than hand-reimplementing syn's own print_qpath logic (trait-vs-rest segment position via qself.position, optional `as Trait`). This matches this function's own explicitly documented policy (its module doc comment: 'rarer shapes ... fall back to quote's raw token-stream rendering, which is still deterministic, just less manicured') and avoids the real risk of a subtly-wrong hand reimplementation of position-based segment splitting, which syn's own vendored print_qpath function already gets right.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: type_spelling no longer collapses a qualified/associated-type path's qualifying type: a Type::Path with a Some qself now falls back to syn's own raw token-stream rendering (which includes the qself type), so two genuinely different qualified paths with different qself types never spell to the same string.
